column1: # Lumeni -- invented here, for this. It has a grammar, because a made-up
# language without one is noise with a font on it.
#   Nouns end -a        luma   light        veka   picture
#   Verbs end -i        lumi   to light     veki   to show
#   Adjectives end -o   lumo   bright       niro   dark
#   Compounds put the modifier FIRST, German-fashion: vekamira, picture-watcher.
# Roots: lum light - vek picture - son sound - ret net - tok time - kor core
#   dek deck - mir see - sen send - hal hold - nir dark - pon ready - tam whole
#   kis small - zar fast - ran edge - fes open - klu shut - gra write - set change
#   nov new - gur keep - ala all - kae place - tir pull - dor door/way
#   bat button - fen window - kan channel - num number - por gate/port
#   kar box - hup help - pik choose - buf store - pen wait - lis hear
#   tal count - jan device - hol word - mun origin - vel copy - lan place-on
#   sov concerning - dop facing - pat body/assembly - mun source
#   Suffix -wia is the one who does it: grawia, writer (the encoder).
#   Numerals: una dua tria kwara; beyond four the interface uses digits.
#   Speech: mi I/me, tu you, pel can, muna before, novtok next/again.
#   halpen rest (held waiting), lumtok day, kistok minute, kisvek pixel.
#   patakora action, batjana push-button device, batrana shortcut.
#   ni exclamation of pain, tokispen pause (wait a little), tiriset move.
# THE LUMENI (made up with the language, 2026-11-05). Lamp-keepers and
# projectionists of the islands in the Niro Sea, where night lasts half the
# year, so light is what they make and trade. Their elders are the vekamira,
# picture-watchers. Every house has a vekafena, a picture-window, and to
# leave one dark is rude. They greet with "Lumi!" (shine!) and part with
# "Lumtok!" (to the day). The great feast is Tamluma at midwinter, when
# every screen on every island is lit at once -- their TAKE ALL. They drink
# lumsona, a tea that glows faintly, and eat kisveka, little picture-biscuits
# stamped with a frame. Silence is a misfortune (vasona); a dark screen is a
# worse one (vaveka). Their sea is full of veka-fish that only surface when
# a screen is lit, which is the excuse given for most things.

column1: That colour is doing something. I don't know what. I love it.
column2: Luma hen cori. Vaisti. Mi meli.

column1: An effect, a ~ and a colour. The critic is crying, skapi. Good crying, I think.
column2: Effect, ~, luma. Vekamira nira-sona, skapi. Maro.

column1: Stack a few. Each has its own ~ on every knob. That is how a look becomes a performance.
column2: Tiri zaro. Ala bata ~. Sui veka ah show.

column1: It's still a square. But it's YOUR square. Post it.
Coach Marv explains sport by drawing circles on it. Once he circled the sun. Ten minutes, skapi.
column2: Coach Marv holi sport so gra rodwenku. Una tok gra rodwen kae lumtoka. Kistok pae, skapi.

column1: Tonight: test patterns, the video synth, and drawing on the picture. Press START.
column2: Lumtok: vekareta, video synth, gra kae veka. Tiri START.

column1: Get me a picture and a pen. BOOM.
Line up the screens BEFORE the show. Not during. I learned this in Plovdiv.
column2: Seti vekadekaku MUNA show. Va kae show. Mi gura kae Plovdiv.

column1: Every desk needs a test pattern. PATTERN adds Pocket Test: checked against real meters.
column2: Ala deka: vekareta. VEKARETA tiri Pocket Test: miren.

column1: He says 'no camera needed' like it is a feature. It is a feature.
My favourite. SOURCE, then Video Synth: oscillators, mirrors and feedback. No camera needed.
column2: Mi meli. MUNGA, novtok Video Synth: oscillator, lumafena, feedback. Vacamera.

column1: Select it, then TAKE. Confident operators press Enter.
column2: Piki, novtok TAKE. Operator zaro tiri Enter.

column1: That's our replay. Every replay needs a pundit.
column2: Hen veka novtok. Ala veka novtok pel holawia.

column1: Now here's a replay. And here's a guy. And BOOM, he's in it.
column2: Hen veka. Hen pata. So BOOM, kae.

column1: Ink goes on top, on its own layer. Press the + at the end of the playlist tabs.
column2: Gra-luma ama, kae layer. Tiri + kae rana vekaku.

column1: A second playlist is a layer over the first. Like a second oscillator, mixed on top.
column2: Vekaku dua: layer ama una. Sui oscillator dua.

column1: In the new playlist: SOURCE, then Draw. Clear everywhere you have not drawn.
column2: Kae vekaku nova: MUNGA, novtok Draw. Lumo kae vagra.

column1: A Draw cue is transparent outside the ink, so the synth shows through.
column2: Draw cue lumo kae vagra, so synth mira.

column1: Select the Draw cue and TAKE it. Two playlists, two layers, one picture.
column2: Piki Draw cue, TAKE. Vekaku dua, layer dua, veka una.

column1: Now both are live: the synth underneath, the ink on top.
column2: Novtok dua kae luma: synth nu, gra ama.

column1: Press DRAW in the inspector, then draw on the programme monitor. Mouse, or a pen if you have one.
column2: Tiri DRAW kae inspector, gra kae program. Mouse, va gra-bata.

column1: A pen's pressure makes the line thicker. A mouse presses at one strength. Like me.
column2: Gra-bata tir: hola tamo. Mouse: rapo. Sui mi.

column1: Circle him! No, bigger. BOOM. That's a cloud. Fine. Circle the cloud.
column2: Rodwen! Va, tamo! BOOM. Luma-nira. Maro. Rodwen luma-nira.

column1: SAVE STILL keeps the drawing as a picture with a clear background, and adds it to the playlist.
column2: SAVE STILL guri gra, veka lumo, so tiri kae vekaku.

column1: For next week's show. Coach Marv will want the cloud again.
column2: Go show novtoka. Coach Marv peni luma-nira.

column1: Patterns, the synth, a layer, ink, a still. Nazdrave, skapi.
column2: Vekareta, synth, layer, gra, vekahala. Nazdrave, skapi.

column1: Try Replay in the Draw section: it draws your lines back the way you drew them.
column2: Tiri Replay kae Draw: gra novtok sui tu gra.

column1: Same time next week. Bring a bigger pen. And a turducken.
column2: Toka rapo novtok. Gra-bata tamo. So kisveka.

column1: The Bureau of Unexplained Signals. Two agents, one photo, and it must not air. Press START.
column2: Kara sona vaisto. Mirawia dua, veka una, vasena. Tiri START.

column1: Masks cut a picture into shapes. Tonight we cut evidence.
column2: Mask: veka dagi. Lumtok: dagi veka-holo.

column1: That's a craft, Brandt. Look at the lights. I want to believe.
column2: Kaira, Brandt. Mira luma. Mi peni isti.

column1: In the inspector's MASK section: mask, then 'new heart'. Any shape will do. The heart is funnier.
column2: Kae MASK inspector: mask, novtok 'new heart'. Ala maro. Inda: lalo.

column1: The library has circles, stars, hearts. Each one is points you can move.
column2: Bufa: rodwen, lumaku, inda. Ala: rana tiriset.

column1: A heart, Hollis? The Bureau redacts with black bars.
column2: Inda, Hollis? Kara niri so nira.

column1: Set the tool to pen, then click round the saucer on the monitor. Click the first point to close it.
column2: Piki gra-bata, so tiri kae ganol. Tiri una, so klui.

column1: Click for corners, drag for curves. The way the Bezier brothers intended.
column2: Tiri go rana, tira go rhaw. Sui Bézier.

column1: Draw round it carefully. It might be watching.
Invert keeps the outside and cuts the inside. The saucer goes. The sky stays.
column2: Seti: gura ar, dagi kae. Ganol gwani. Lumtoka gura.

column1: The same shape, the other way round. Very useful. Slightly spooky.
Hollis, there's a heart-shaped hole in the sky.
Feather softens the edge, so nobody sees the cut. Press + on feather.
column2: Ranakiso: vamira dag. Tiri + kae feather.

column1: A hard edge says 'someone was here'. A soft one says nothing at all.
column2: Rana tamo: 'una kae hen'. Rana kiso: vahola.

column1: A library shape, the pen, invert and feather. The Bureau thanks you. The Bureau was never here.
column2: Kar bufa, gra-bata, seti, ranakiso. Kara holi lumo. Kara vakae hen.

column1: Masks also go on a layer, an output, or its matte: MASK ON chooses. And every control takes a ~.
column2: Mask kae layer, senadora, matte: MASK ON piki. Ala bata ~.

column1: The truth is in the waveform, Hollis. Next time, the scopes.
column2: Isto kae waveform, Hollis. Novtok: scope.

column1: A lighthouse, a ghost, and a keeper who has been alone with the lamp far too long. Press START.
column2: Lumafena, gaur, so luma-gurwia kae lumaka tok tamo. Tiri START.

column1: Projection mapping: bending the picture to fit the building. Warp, blend, slices.
column2: Projection mapping: seti veka go barada. Warp, sonaveka, kisaka.

column1: Ye'll be wanting the ghost on the windows. Mind the lamp. The lamp is MINE.
column2: Gaur kae fenaku, ha? Mira luma. Luma MI!

column1: MENU, then Video Outputs, then Geometry. Where an output's shape lives.
column2: MENU, novtok Vekasenaku, novtok Geometry. Hen kae senadora kar.

column1: Geometry: the projector-menu word for 'what shape is the picture'.
Press warp edit, then drag a corner on the programme monitor. The window is not square. Neither is the keeper.
column2: Tiri warp edit, so tiri rana kae program. Fena vakar. Luma-gurwia vakar.

column1: A corner pin moves the four corners. Perspective keeps the lines straight, like a real window.
column2: Rana-pin: rana kwara tiriseti. Lino tiro, sui fena.

column1: LEFT! Ye call that a corner? I've seen straighter gulls.
column2: LAA! Rana? Mi mira gwael tiro.

column1: Back in Geometry: edge blend, + on the left and + on the right.
column2: Novtok Geometry: edge blend, + laa so + rana.

column1: Two projectors overlap; each fades its edge so the overlap is not twice as bright.
column2: Projector dua; ala ranakiso, so valuma dua.

column1: Geometry, SLICES, open. The Screens window is where slices are cut and placed.
column2: Geometry, SLICES, fesi. Screens: kisaka dagi so lana.

column1: A slice is a piece of the picture, put anywhere on the output.
column2: Kisaka: veka kiso, ala kae senadora.

column1: In the Screens window, + SLICE three times, and drag each crop to a third of the picture.
column2: Kae Screens, + SLICE tria, so tiri ala go veka tria-una.

column1: Three windows, three slices: left, middle and right of one picture.
column2: Fena tria, kisaka tria: laa, enedh, rana.

column1: Three windows. The lamp gets the middle one. The lamp ALWAYS gets the middle one.
column2: Fena tria. Enedh: luma. Enedh ALATOK luma.

column1: Warp, blend, slices. The keeper will finally sleep. The gulls will not.
column2: Warp, sonaveka, kisaka. Luma-gurwia hali. Gwael vahali.

column1: Slices have their own warp and mesh in the Screens window. And a ~ on the place and the turn.
column2: Kisaka: warp so mesh kae Screens. So ~ kae kaea so seta.

column1: Ye did alright, lad. Now get away from the lamp.
column2: Maro, kisapata. Novtok: tira mun luma.

column1: A game show, skapi. Three contestants, one buzzer, and cues that fire from anywhere. Press START.
column2: Numa-show, skapi. Patku tria, buzzer una, cue mun ala kae. Tiri START.

column1: Cue numbers, hotkeys, and GO from other machines. Like a sequencer you can play from any key.
column2: Cue numa, batrana, so GO mun karajana novo. Sui sequencer.

column1: Welcome to the show! Let's spin that wheel!
Contestant 3 is selected. In the inspector's metadata, give it a cue number: 3.
Theatre numbers its cues. Q3, Q3.5, Q12A. Deckboy reads them all.
column2: Lammaka numi cue. Q3, Q3.5, Q12A. Deckboy miri ala.

column1: I'd like to buy a number, please.
Ctrl+G, type the number, Enter. It goes live wherever the list happens to be standing.
column2: Ctrl+G, gra numa, Enter. Go luma, ala kae.

column1: GOTO. The fastest way across a long list. Faster than scrolling. Much faster than me.
column2: GOTO. Dora zaro kae holaku tamo. Zaro. Zaro muna mi.

column1: Contestant 1 is selected. In TRIGGERS, press key, then F5. That key now fires this cue.
column2: Pata 1 piken. Kae TRIGGERS: key, novtok F5. Bata hen tiri cue hen.

column1: F1 to F10, F12, or the number pad. Each one, a buzzer.
column2: F1 go F10, F12, va numa-bata. Ala: buzzer.

column1: Press the key. The cue fires, wherever the list is standing.
column2: Tiri bata. Cue lumi, ala kae.

column1: No mouse, no list, no looking. Just the key.
Companion, a MIDI note, an OSC message: MENU, then Network, says where each one connects.
column2: Companion, MIDI, OSC: MENU, novtok Reta, holi kae.

column1: A Stream Deck in the next room can press GO. So can a keyboard synth. I prefer the synth.
column2: Stream Deck kae kaea novo pel GO. Synth je. Mi meli synth.

column1: And for our viewers at home: you can play along too.
column2: So mirawia kae kaea: tu pel je!

column1: Numbers, GOTO, a buzzer, and GO from anywhere. You are a game show now, skapi.
column2: Numa, GOTO, buzzer, GO mun ala kae. Novtok tu numa-show, skapi.

column1: A cue can have a key, a MIDI note and an OSC address at once. Belt, braces and a second belt.
column2: Cue: bata, MIDI, OSC, unatok. Gura, gura, so gura novo.

column1: Channel 6 weather, skapi. A map, a presenter, and a very large lizard. Press START.
column2: Lumtoka kae Kana 6, skapi. Kara, holawia, so lizka tamo. Veka-fish kae Niro, so kaiju. Tiri START.

column1: Words on screen: Lower Thirds, text, and backdrops.
column2: Hola kae vekadeka: Lower Third, hola, dopa.

column1: I'm June O'Neil, and nothing about this forecast is normal.
column2: Mi June O'Neil. Lumtoka hen vamaro.

column1: Words go on their own layer: press the + at the end of the playlist tabs.
column2: Hola kae layer: tiri + kae rana vekaku.

column1: A second playlist is a layer over the map. The lizard stays underneath. Mostly.
column2: Vekaku dua: layer ama kara. Lizka nu. Tamo.

column1: Words on top. Always on top.
In the new playlist: SOURCE, then Lower Third.
column2: Kae vekaku nova: MUNGA, novtok Lower Third.

column1: A name and a title, low on the screen, out of the lizard's way.
column2: Hola so pata, nu kae vekadeka, mun lizka.

column1: In the inspector, title: type the presenter's name. The second line is her job.
column2: Kae inspector, title: gra hola holawia. Lino dua: pata hin.

column1: Spelling counts. The audience reads it at the speed of light.
Spell it right. Last week it said 'Jane O'Meal'.
TAKE the Lower Third. Her name slides in over the map.
column2: TAKE Lower Third. Hola tiriseti ama kara.

column1: Two layers live: the weather, and the words on top of it.
column2: Layer dua kae luma: lumtoka, hola ama.

column1: Thank you. Now, about that lizard...
SOURCE, then Text: a title card. Then its backdrop chip: key green, for the vision mixer to key out.
column2: MUNGA, novtok Text: kara-veka. Novtok dopa: luma-lumo, go mixer.

column1: A backdrop fills behind the words. Key green or key blue, and the mixer does the rest.
column2: Dopa: nu hola. Luma-lumo va luma-luin, mixer cori.

column1: Breaking news: it's standing on the five-day forecast.
column2: Hola novo: lizka kae lumtoka pae.

column1: A Lower Third, a name, a title card, a backdrop. The lizard has left the studio, skapi.
column2: Lower Third, hola, kara-veka, dopa. Lizka gwani, skapi.

column1: Lower Thirds can wait, slide and leave on their own. Their section has every setting.
column2: Lower Third: peni, tiriseti, gwani. Ala kae sona hin.

column1: That's the weather. Back to you, guys. Run.
column2: Lumtoka tamo. Novtok kae kara. Zari!

column1: A rocket built in a basement, skapi, and an inventor who wants cheese. Press START.
column2: Kaira kae kara-nu, skapi, so korwia peni cheese. Tiri START.

column1: Stage timers: countdowns, clocks, and a presenter view for the person on stage.
column2: Toka-tala: nu, toka, so mira go holawia.

column1: Cheese, Grommet! The moon's made of it. We'll need a countdown.
column2: Cheese, Grommet! Luna: cheese. Peni tala nu.

column1: SOURCE, then Stage Timer. A clock that counts down, in big friendly numbers.
column2: MUNGA, novtok Stage Timer. Toka tala nu, numa tamo.

column1: Its colours change as it runs out: white, amber, red. Like a VU meter for time.
column2: Luma seti: lumo, malo, rado. VU go toka.

column1: Select the timer and TAKE it. The countdown starts.
Past zero it keeps going, counting the overtime. Very honest. Slightly rude.
Ten... nine... ooh, I do love a countdown.
column2: Pae... neder... ai, mi meli tala nu.

column1: Something's loose! Space holds the countdown. The clock shows it is held.
A hold is not a stop. Space again, and it carries on from where it was.
column2: Hali vameth. Space novtok, so tala.

column1: MENU, Video Outputs: make an output's type PRESENTER. The person on stage gets the timer, the next cue and their notes.
column2: MENU, Vekasenaku: senadora PRESENTER. Holawia mira toka, cue novtoko, so hola.

column1: A presenter view is an output like any other. Point it at the confidence monitor.
So the pilot can see the time. The pilot is Grommet.
A countdown, a hold, and a view for the pilot. Nazdrave, skapi. Bring crackers.
column2: Tala nu, hali, mira go pata-zara. Nazdrave, skapi. Tiri kisveka.

column1: Timers can also count up, or show the time of day. Their section has the lot.
column2: Toka-tala ama so nu, so toka. Ala kae.

column1: A grand day out, Grommet! Pass the crackers.
A magic show, skapi. A trunk, a prop, and one beat where everything changes at once. Press START.
column2: Gûl-show, skapi. Kara, pata-veka, so toka una: ala seti. Tiri START.

column1: Two playlists are two layers. TAKE ALL changes both together.
column2: Vekaku dua: layer dua. TAKE ALL: dua seti, unatok. Tamluma kisa!

column1: Every trick needs two things happening at once. And a rubber chicken.
column2: Ala gûl: dua unatok. So kara-pila gumo.

column1: The prop goes on its own layer. Press the + at the end of the playlist tabs.
column2: Pata-veka kae layer. Tiri + kae rana vekaku.

column1: Playlist 2 sits on top of playlist 1. Like a transparency on an overhead projector.
Nothing up my sleeve. Everything in my trunk.
column2: Vanakae kae hamp. Ala kae kara.

column1: In the new playlist, add anything: PATTERN will do. That is the prop.
column2: Kae vekaku nova, tiri ala: VEKARETA maro. Hen pata-veka.

column1: Whatever it is, it will appear the instant the trunk opens.
Is it a rubber chicken? It's always a rubber chicken.
Select 'The trunk (open)' in playlist 1 and the prop in playlist 2. Then TAKE ALL: both on one beat.
column2: Piki 'Kara (fesa)' kae vekaku 1 so pata-veka kae vekaku 2. Novtok TAKE ALL: unatok. Tamluma!

column1: One press, every playlist's selected cue. The audience never sees the seam.
column2: Tiri una, ala cue. Mirawia vamira rana.

column1: Two layers, one beat. Every playlist has its own opacity and can sit on any output. Nazdrave, skapi.
column2: Layer dua, toka una. Ala vekaku: lumo hin, ala senadora. Nazdrave, skapi.

column1: A magician never reveals. A playlist never minds being revealed.
Thank you! I'm here all week! The chicken is here forever.
column2: Lumtok! Mi kae hen! Pila: alatok.

column1: A cooking show, skapi. Live. Everything is on fire. Press START.
column2: Mira-show, skapi. Lumo. Ala lumi! Tiri START.

column1: BLACK hides the picture and keeps the show running. PANIC stops everything. Know which you need.
column2: BLACK niri veka, show sena. PANIC hali ala. Isti.

column1: Bork bork! Hurdy-flurdy, de kitchen is fire-a-flurdy!
The audience must not see this. Press BLACK, or B.
column2: Mirawia vamira! Tiri BLACK, va B.

column1: The picture goes. The cue keeps playing underneath, ready to come back.
Bork? Bork. Oh, de picture is gun.
The fire's out. Press B again: the picture comes back, still running.
column2: Luma nira. Tiri B: veka novtok.

column1: Nothing was lost. A mute on a mixer, for pictures.
Worse: MENU, System, the SAFETY card: PANIC. Everything stops, the way the panic setting says.
column2: Nirako: MENU, Kora, SAFETY: PANIC. Ala hali.

column1: PANIC is the big red button. Use it when BLACK is not enough. Then breathe.
column2: PANIC: bata rado tamo. Tok BLACK vamaro. Novtok thui.

column1: Close MENU, select the souffle, and TAKE it. The show is back on.
column2: Klui MENU, piki soufflé, TAKE. Show novtok.

column1: After a panic, the show is still there. Pick up where you meant to be.
Voila! De souffle, he is risen!
BLACK to hide, PANIC to stop, TAKE to come back. You will survive any kitchen, skapi.
column2: BLACK niri, PANIC hali, TAKE novtok. Tu gura ala kaea, skapi.

column1: The panic setting chooses what PANIC does: fade out, cut, or just the outputs.
Presets, skapi. A whole look, remembered, and back with one button. Press START.
column2: Preset, skapi. Veka tamo, guren, novtok bata una. Tiri START.

column1: Like the patch memory on a synth: store, then recall.
Press DASH: buttons of your own, for anything at all.
Ctrl+D also works. Very fast. Very professional.
Press +, then 'preset - a new preset from what is on now'. The button remembers this look.
column2: Tiri +, novtok 'preset - a new preset from what is on now'. Bata gura veka.

column1: Store. Like saving the patch before the drummer leans on the synth.
Close the DASH (Esc), then select Look two and TAKE it. A different look.
column2: Klui DASH (Esc), piki Veka dua, TAKE. Veka novo.

column1: Change it all. Don't worry. It remembers.
Open the DASH and press your preset button. The first look comes back.
column2: Fesi DASH, tiri bata. Veka una novtok.

column1: Recall. The patch memory, returning. Beautiful.
A look, stored and recalled. A preset can keep cues, positions, effects, levels and routing; its button's menu chooses which.
column2: Veka guren so piken. Preset gura cue, kaea, effect; bata menu piki.

column1: And a DASH button can run any command at all. Any. Even the exciting ones.
A space-opera trailer, skapi. A narrator with a very deep voice and opinions about transitions. Press START.
column2: Trailer, skapi. Holawia sona tamo. Tiri START.

column1: A transition is how one cue becomes the next. There are far more than the crossfade.
column2: Seta: cue ah cue novtoko. Zaro muna lumseta.

column1: In a galaxy of content... one operator... must choose a transition.
column2: Kae lumaka-nira... operator una... piki seta.

column1: 'The planet' is selected. In the inspector, its transition style: choose iris.
Pushes, wipes, iris, dip to white. Even a portal. I wrote half of them. On a Tuesday.
column2: Seta: iris, lumo. Portal je. Mi gra. Kae lumtok dua.

column1: The planet deserves... a dramatic entrance.
Give it a time: + on transition until it says a second or more.
No time, no transition. A style needs a duration to do anything at all.
TAKE the planet. Watch it arrive.
The transition belongs to the cue arriving. Each cue chooses its own entrance.
column2: Seta: go cue novo. Ala cue piki.

column1: Now 'The battle': choose shatter, give it a time, and TAKE it.
Shatter drops the old picture like a pane of glass. Please do not do this at a funeral.
column2: Shatter: veka gwani sui fena. Vakae nira-sona!

column1: A style, a time, and two very dramatic entrances. Nazdrave, skapi.
column2: Dopa, toka, so lumi dua. Nazdrave, skapi.

column1: A playlist has a default style too, for every cue that does not choose its own.
Coming soon... to a desk near you.
Two robot DJs, skapi. They do not talk. Their helmets do. Press START.
column2: DJ korpata dua, skapi. Vaholi. Mivku holi. Tiri START.

column1: Every cue has its own chain of audio effects, and some of them break the sound on purpose.
column2: Ala cue: sona effect. Novo dagi sona.

column1: > HELLO. WE ARE HERE TO FIX YOUR MIX.
The beat is selected. In its AUDIO EFFECTS section, + adds one. Try the delay.
column2: Sona-tala piken. AUDIO EFFECTS, +. Tiri delay.

column1: Delay, reverb, filters, a compressor. Amount always means 'less of this'.
> ONE MORE TIME. WITH ECHO. ECHO. ECHO.
Add a second: a bend, like crush. It damages the sound the way a broken file would.
column2: Tiri dua: rhaw, crush. Dagi sona sui kara ni.

column1: The bends are my favourite. Like a tape left in the sun. On purpose.
column2: Rhaw: mi meli. Sui tape kae lumtoka.

column1: MENU, then Audio: where each playlist's sound goes, and the patch for named outputs.
column2: MENU, novtok Sona: ala sona kae.

column1: Speakers, monitors, an in-ear for the drummer. The patch sends each its own.
column2: Sona-jana, monitor, in-ear. Patch sena ala.

column1: > AROUND THE MIX. AROUND THE MIX. AROUND THE MIX.
column2: > RODWEN SONA. RODWEN SONA. RODWEN SONA.

column1: An effect, a bend and the patch. The robots approve, skapi. I think. Their faces are helmets.
column2: Effect, rhaw, patch. Korpata lumo, skapi. Miv.

column1: Every audio effect can follow a ~ too, even Motion. Wave at the delay. It's wonderful.
column2: Ala sona effect ~, Motion je. Hel go delay. Lumo.

column1: > THANK YOU. GOOD NIGHT. WE ARE ROBOTS.
The Bureau again, skapi. A glow on the horizon, and two agents who disagree about it. Press START.
column2: Kara novtok, skapi. Luma kae rana, so mirawia dua vaholi. Tiri START.

column1: The scopes measure a picture: brightness, colour, levels. Numbers, not opinions.
column2: Scope miri veka: luma, luma-ran. Numa, vahola.

column1: It's them, Brandt. It's a craft. Look how it glows.
The scopes read only what really goes out, never a preview. Turn the output on: MENU, Video Outputs, OUTPUT OFF.
column2: Scope miri sena isto, vamuna-veka. Lumi senadora: MENU, Vekasenaku, SENADORA NIRO.

column1: Measuring a scaled-down preview would be measuring a photocopy. We measure the original.
column2: Miri veka kiso: sui vela. Mi miri muna.

column1: Chain of evidence, Hollis. The real signal or nothing.
column2: Dora veka-holo, Hollis. Sena isto, va nakae.

column1: Close MENU. Above the monitor, the PROGRAM button: press it until it says SCOPES or BOTH.
column2: Klui MENU. Ama monitor, PROGRAM: tiri, tok SCOPES va BOTH.

column1: Both shows the picture and its scopes side by side. Very civilised.
Click the waveform to make it big. Bright things sit high, dark things low, left to right as in the picture.
column2: Tiri waveform: tamo. Lumo ama, niro nu.

column1: Fields per rendered frame. 1 is one for one, 0.5 holds each field for two frames, 0 freezes it.
column2: Patku veka. 1 una una, 0.5 hali dua, 0 hali tam.

column1: What this cue shows while it plays: waveform, scope, Lissajous, spectrum, meters or a name card
column2: Ma miri veka nakae: vonda, scope, Lissajous, spectrum, mirku nu kara hol

column2: 0 piki kara sov luma, veka mira. 1 piki vapika, reta forma.

column1: How far it travels, in semitones. Up reads as arrival, down as departure, zero is a struck note.

column1: Alternating mirrors by cell position, which reads as pattern where random flipping reads as noise.

column1: The whole gesture. This IS the cue's duration -- a sting is the one generated signal here that ends.
column2: Tirisa tama. NAKAE tok veka -- sting una tamo.

column2: Pixel sort: kisvekku sov luma kae hola, datamosh lumso.

column1: How many cells the marks may climb. They thin out as they go, so a tall reach trails rather than doubles.
column2: Tal kara rankku ala. Kiso kae ala, va dua.

column1: Reference pitch. 440 is modern standard, 432 the common alternative, and older instruments sat lower still.
column2: Sonala muna. 440 nova, 432 dua, jana muno nira.

column2: Kae sting muni. Nira hola, kisi; ala kae, dopi.

column1: Quarter turns are exact and stay crisp. Spinning samples at an angle, which tears pixel art -- sometimes that is what you want.
column2: Kora kwara tamo & lumo. Kora ala kuka pixel art -- nu tu veli.

column1: Every take starts the puppetry the same way, so a rehearsed look repeats instead of depending on how long the app has been open.

column1: What aims each tilt: its own position, the picture's luma gradient so characters lean the way the image does, or the cell's hue.

column2: Bati kan: klua, 0, -3, -6, -12 dB. Tiri ran dop nivela. Vekaku vana dop jana sova.

column1: Internal resolution, 1 chunkiest to 5 finest. This is an aesthetic control as much as a speed one -- the 8-bit look comes from big pixels.
column2: Veka dora, 1 kiso dop 5 tamo. Forma sov zara -- 8-bit kae kisvekku tamo.

column1: Picture takes colour from the image. Green, amber and cyan are terminal phosphors. Palette locks the text to the selected hardware palette.
column2: Picture tiri luma veka. Verda, lumora & cyan lumaku tok muna. Palette hali hola kae luma jana.

column1: SUBTLE self-heals (H.264). CLASSIC is the real smear (MPEG-4). EXTREME is chunkier and smears constantly. Changing this re-prepares the cue.
column2: SUBTLE lumi sova (H.264). CLASSIC niri tamo (MPEG-4). EXTREME tamo & niri ala. Seti poni veka.

column1: Equal temperament buys free modulation at the cost of every interval being slightly wrong. Just and pythagorean are exactly in tune in one key. Bohlen-Pierce divides a twelfth, so it has no octaves.
column2: Equal temperament: ala sona kis vaso. Just & pythagorean tamo kae una. Bohlen-Pierce vana octave.

column2: Doptala, hala, tirmira so tirisena. Seni kisveka.

column1: A magic show, skapi. A trunk, a rubber chicken, and one beat where everything changes at once. Press START.
column2: Gul-show, skapi. Kara, falo korpata, so una toka kae ala seti. Bati TIRI.

column1: Two playlists are two layers, and TAKE ALL changes both together. Tonight you will see why that matters.
column2: Vekaku dua pataku dua, so TAKE ALL seti dua unatok. Nirtok nakae tu miri kora.

column1: The chicken goes on its own layer. Press the + at the end of the playlist tabs.
column2: Korpata kae una pata. Bati + kae rana vekaku-tabku.

column1: The lit tab is the playlist that gets the next cue. Its chip now says 'to Out 1': it is layered over playlist 1 on that output.
column2: Lumo taba vekaku go nov veka. Chip novtok holi 'go Sena 1': pata jora vekaku 1 kae nakae senador.

column1: Turnip Top has put the chicken in playlist 2. In playlist 1, TAKE 'The trunk (open)'. Then in playlist 2, TAKE the chicken.
column2: Turnip Top lani korpata kae vekaku 2. Kae vekaku 1, SENI 'The trunk (open)'. Novtok kae vekaku 2, SENI korpata.

column1: The chicken is clear all round, so it covers only itself. Watch the monitor between the two TAKEs.
column2: Korpata feno kae ala rana, so hali una na. Miri mirajana kae toka mun SENI dua.

column1: Did you see it? For a moment the trunk was open and empty: two TAKEs are two moments. The trick is reset. Now select the open trunk in playlist 1 and the chicken in playlist 2, then TAKE ALL.
column2: Tu miri? Kistoka kara feso so vaka: SENI dua tokaku dua. Gul pono novtok. Piki feso kara kae vekaku 1 so korpata kae vekaku 2, novtok TAKE ALL.

column1: TAKE ALL takes every playlist's selected cue on one beat. No gap, no empty trunk.
column2: TAKE ALL seni piko veka mun ala vekaku kae unatok. Varanka, vakara vaka.

column1: The chicken was late. They saw an empty trunk. In magic we call that a trunk.
column2: Korpata tok-dopo. Na miri vaka kara. Kae gul, mi so tu holi nakae kara.

column1: Trick two. Drag playlist 2's opacity fader down to nothing. The chicken fades away.
column2: Gul dua. Tiri vekaku 2 lumanuma rana go 0. Korpata niri kistok.

column1: Every playlist has its own opacity. Down is a fade out, with no cue at all.
column2: Una vekaku guri una lumanuma. Dop niri kistok, vaveka nova.

column1: Ta-daaa! ...Hold for applause. Hold. Now watch it go.
column2: Ta-daaa! ...Peni patasona. Peni. Novtok miri tiri.

column1: Trick three. Bring it back: playlist 2's opacity all the way up.
column2: Gul tria. Dopi na: vekaku 2 lumanuma tam jora.

column1: Where did it go? Back in the trunk. Everything goes back in the trunk.
column2: Na tiri kae kena? Dop kae kara. Ala dopi kae kara.

column1: An appearance done wrong, then right, a vanish and a return. Nazdrave.
column2: Fesi vavo, novtok isto, niri so dopi. Nazdrave.

column1: A playlist can also sit on any output. Two layers, a great many tricks.
column2: Vekaku pel lani kae ala senador. Pataku dua, gulaku tam.

column1: It's back! Thank you! I'm here all week! The chicken is here forever.
column2: Na dopi! Lumi! Mi nakae tam heptoka! Korpata nakae tamtoka!

column1: A cooking show, skapi. Live. The kitchen is on fire. Press START.
column2: Sonapena-show, skapi. Lumo. Sonapenakara nirlumi. Bati TIRI.

column1: Bork! De fire extinguisher is also on fire!
BLACK to hide, PANIC to stop, TAKE to come back. You will survive any kitchen.
column2: nira go niri, PANIC go hali, SENI go dopi. Tu pel tiri mun ala sonapenakara.

column1: A fashion show, skapi. One designer, one runway, and a look she will want back. Press START.
column2: Pataveka-show, skapi. Karawia una, rana una, so mira na guri novtok. Bati TIRI.

column1: A preset stores a whole look and brings it back with one button.
column2: Mungura guri tam mira so dopi pel una bat.

column1: Darling. A look is not a look until you can get it back.
column2: Lumami. Mira vamira si tu vapel dopi.

column1: Buttons. Good. I design with buttons.
column2: Batku. Lumo. Mi kari pel batku.

column1: Store it. Before somebody has ideas.
column2: Guri. Muna kena guri nov holaku.

column1: Close the DASH (Esc), then select Look two and TAKE it.
column2: Klui DASH (Esc), piki Look two so SENI.

column1: A cape. On my runway. Someone will trip, darling. Someone always trips.
column2: Doppata. Kae mi rana. Kena niri, lumami. Kena niri ala tok.

column1: Recall: the whole look comes back at once.
Thank you. We will never speak of the cape again.
column2: Lumi. Mi so tu vaholi sov doppata novtok.

column1: Simple. Timeless. Recallable. Now go, darling. I have a fitting.
column2: Kiso. Tamtoko. Dopipelo. Tiri, lumami. Mi guri patamira.

column1: Pushes, wipes, iris, dip to white, and more. I wrote half of them. On a Tuesday.
column2: Tiri, niri, iris, dopi go lumtamo, so novku. Mi gra kora mun na. Kae lumtok tria.

column1: A style, a time, and two very dramatic entrances. Roll credits.
column2: Mira, toka, so tiraku dua tam holako. Tiri ranaholaku.

column1: That is not an iris. ...It is better. I will allow it.
An effect, a bend and the patch. The robots approve, I think. Their faces are helmets.
column2: Effect, rhaw so patch. Korpata poni, mi miri. Na mivku korakaraku.

column1: Waveform, vectorscope, false colour. The scopes settled it. The agents did not.
column2: Waveform, vectorscope, luma-va. Scope piki. Mirawiaku vapiki.

column1: Major Tomasina is in orbit, skapi, and her picture has to reach the ground. Press START.
column2: Major Tomasina tiri rodwo, skapi, so na veka hup sena go kaepata. Bati TIRI.

column1: Pictures leave by cable or network: NDI, SDI from a DeckLink card, ST 2110 for broadcast plants.
column2: Vekaku tiri pel lina va reta: NDI, SDI mun DeckLink karta, ST 2110 go tam senkaraku.

column1: Ground control, this is Major Tomasina. Can you see my picture?
column2: Kae-kora, nakae Major Tomasina. Tu pel miri mi veka?

column1: Every way down, on one page. Good. Space has very few cables.
column2: Ala dorku dop kae una holapena. Lumo. Niro-kara guri kis linaku.

column1: Sending now. If nobody answers, I'll just float here.
column2: Seni novtok. Si kena vaholi, mi hali tiro nakae.

column1: Ground control, signing off. Tell my mother I waved.
column2: Kae-kora, mi klui. Holi go mi muna mi tiriseti pata.

column1: Ground control can see me! I can see my house from here.
column2: Kae-kora pel miri mi! Mi pel miri mi bufa mun nakae.

column1: And one more window, showing the clock. Operators who watch a clock are never late.
column2: So una nov fena, veki toka. Senwia miri toka vatok-dopi.

column1: The big window is window one, which is usually the programme.
column2: Tamo fena una fena, ala-kora KORAVEKA.

column1: Windows, the ... menu, NEXT, the clock, a layout, tally. Mystery solved.
column2: Fenaku, ... menu, NEXT, toka, layout, tally. Isto feso.

column1: FX CHOICE: choice must be A or B
column2: FX CHOICE: pika hup A va B

column1: FX CHOICE: no effect at that index
column2: FX CHOICE: vaeffect kae nakae numa
